pages.title: Resident Evil 4 - Archipelago
lines: Dear {slot},
Welcome to Resident Evil 4 Archipelago (RE4R AP). This mod randomizes the
contents of RE4R amongst all the other games in your Multiworld, set up by
your Archipelago Host. From the Hunter's Lodge onward you will start to see
items appearing as the Archipelago logo. Collecting one sends a Check to
another player in the Multiworld, and their findings send items to you -
weapons, herbs, key items, anything.
WARNING
You may receive a key item early, but using it early may have unintended side
effects, including a softlock. If you're unsure, just proceed through the
playthrough in the intended order.

pages.title: Reporting a Bug
lines: For every bug or issue, open the RE4R AP Wizard and press Generate Bug Report
(bottom right). It packs everything I need into one .zip, which you can send
to me in the Archipelago After Dark Discord, in the Resident Evil 4
discussion:
discord.gg/fqvNCCRsu4
Ideally, do this before you relaunch the game (not viable for a crash,
obviously), since RE4R wipes its log file every time it starts. The Wizard
keeps a copy of the last log it saw, but the freshest evidence is the log from
the run where things went wrong.

pages.title: Starting Arsenal
lines: Unless disabled, you start with 2 random weapons as your Starting Arsenal,
drawn from up to 23 guns: the Merchant's original stock, the three guns found
in the world, the Deluxe and Separate Ways guns that work in Leon's campaign,
and the Bonus Weapons (Handcannon and Chicago Sweeper). The guns you start
with leave the AP pool; the rest are scattered amongst the Multiworld. Your
starting guns can also spawn with attachments. A scope-supported gun starts
with its scope 100% of the time, and every other gun has a 50% chance of one
compatible attachment.
The Bonus Weapons (Handcannon, Chicago Sweeper, and the Primal Knife as the
second knife upgrade) are in the pool like the rest of the Merchant's gear.
The mod stops the game from handing them out for free or deleting them, and
nothing is ever written to your game profile.

pages.title: The Merchant: Buy Tab
lines: - The Merchant deals in Checks now, on both the Buy and Trade tabs.
- With Shuffle Merchant Gear on (the default), everything he sold as gear is
in the AP Pool: weapons, attachments, case upgrades, knives, recipes, body
armor and his trade stock.
- Buy tab Checks cost 2,500 / 7,500 / 15,000 pesetas by tier. Buying another
player's item refunds you 1 / 3 / 6 Spinel, so helping a friend costs money
up front and pays back in trade currency. Your own items are normal spending
and refund nothing.
- New Checks are unlocked at every Chapter. The Buy tab shows at most 20
unbought Checks at once; the rest sit in a queue until you buy more.
- The shop is restocked every Chapter with "Staples" to aid you with healing
and crafting.

pages.title: The Merchant: Trade Tab
lines: - Trade tab Checks cost 1 / 3 / 6 Spinel by tier, on seven tiles that rotate
as you buy.
- Exchange Velvet Blue at 2 Spinel, as often as you like, and the three
gemstones at 3, 4 and 5 Spinel, restocked every Chapter.
- Turn Spinel into money quickly with Velvet Blue, or invest into gems to slot
into your Treasures for a larger profit.
- The Multiworld mints exactly enough Spinel to afford every Trade Check, and
the Merchant's Requests provide more on top of that, so there's a bit of
forgiveness if a Spinel check is left behind.
- A tile with nothing behind it displays the "Claimed" state.
- Trade Checks never refund.

pages.title: Receiving Items
lines: - Items arrive while the game is playable, never mid-load or in a cutscene;
anything sent while you're not in a "playable" state is queued until you are
- Guns, grenades, and knives go to typewriter Storage, never your case.
- Ammo, health, gunpowder and resources go into your case; if it is full, or
nothing fits, they go to Storage too.
- Key items, tokens, charms and recipes reach the Key Items tab, treasures the
Treasure tab, Pesetas and Spinel your wallet.
- Case upgrades and knives are progressive: each Progressive Attache Case is
the next size up from the one you carry, each Progressive Knife the next
knife you do not own (the Fighting Knife, then the Primal).

pages.title: Typewriters
lines: You're likely familiar with the Typewriters spread out across the world of
RE4R, like the one beside this note. They save your game - you're encouraged
to save often. AP items you send out and receive are saved and mirrored by the
AP server, but any "normal" items in RE4R will be lost, just like normal
progression.
Typewriters also allow you to Warp back to them once discovered (or from the
start, if your settings file unlocked them). Be warned that this should be a
last resort, and is known to have issues with unloaded areas, strange
lighting, etc.

pages.title: REFramework, Menus, & Displays
lines: Press Insert at any time to open the Archipelago window (this is REFramework's
toggle key, which will hide/show menus at any time).
The UI Overlay sits in the top right corner and always shows your current
Chapter, Area & number of Checks you have found there.
The Checklist tab is your hub for progress across everything in the room: the
Main Campaign, The Mercenaries, and (eventually) Separate Ways. The bar at the
top counts every Check found against every Check the room holds. Below it,
each content has its own section with its own count and bar. Main Campaign
lists every Typewriter & the Checks near it. Open a Typewriter to see the
Chapters & Areas it covers, and a Warp button. Merchant and Mercenaries each
have their own sections as well.

pages.title: REFramework, Menus, & Displays (continued)
lines: The Guidance tab controls various assistance features that come with RE4R AP.
Unchecked AP item locations show a floating [AP] Marker with the distance, the
chapter it belongs to, and how far above or below you it is. The Guidance tab
allows you to turn Markers on or off, adjust how far away they appear, and
make them more or less detailed. You may also view this Tutorial again at any
time inside the Guidance tab.
The Hints tab spends hint points to learn where an item is. Hints for items in
your world will automatically show their [AP] Marker, while Hints about your
items in other worlds get pinned on screen under Multiworld Hints. Multiworld
Hints can be hidden in the Guidance tab.
Something's Wrong has recovery tools if a Check refuses to send. If you've run
into a bug or issue of some kind, you're encouraged to report it in the
Discord with a bug report generated from inside the Wizard (bottom right).

pages.title: Debug Tab & Developer Tools
lines: The Debug tab is hidden by default and nothing in it is needed to play. To
show it, open the REFramework menu (Insert), find ArchipelagoRE4R under Script
Generated UI, and tick "Developer Tools (Debug tab)".
The one tool you may need is Item Injection. If an item another player sent
you never arrived, first reconnect from the Server tab: the mod re-delivers
anything it missed. If it is still not there, open Item Injection. The items
you were sent most recently sit under Recent, one button each; anything else
you can find by Category and name. Set the Count, press Inject Item, and the
Status line tells you where it landed. Only inject what the Multiworld
actually sent you.
The rest of the tab is for the people fixing bugs. One warning: the DeathLink
simulation really does kill you.

pages.title: The Mercenaries
lines: If your settings file includes The Mercenaries, the mode is part of your
Multiworld. Each character and stage pair has rank Checks (Rank A always; S,
S+ and S++ depending on your settings), and the characters and stages
themselves are the items: one of each starts with you, the rest stay locked
until their item arrives. Only Rank A can hold anything another player needs,
so no seed depends on a top score.
Campaign items that arrive while you are in The Mercenaries wait until you are
back in the campaign. A room can also be Mercenaries only, with no campaign at
all; the goal is then Rank A on every character and stage combination.

pages.title: Keys, Drawers and Ashley
lines: By default, Small Keys stay in your own world, each placed no later than the
drawer it opens. A locked drawer is never waiting on another player. If Small
Keys get shuffled into other Worlds, it's possible they could get to you after
you pass the drawer.
While you play as Ashley, her own keys reach her directly, even mid-section.
Everything else waits until you are Leon again.

pages.title: Known Issues
lines: - Some pickups can grant the item and send nothing. The tell is an Archipelago
logo left in your inventory. Force Check it in Something's Wrong and report
the location.
- A key sent by another player can vanish from a door's "use" list before the
door opens. The mod puts it back on offer while you stand at the door
holding it. If the door still refuses, report it; your host can open the way
from the room's console.
- Typewriter Warps can land you in an area that has not finished loading, with
odd lighting or missing objects. Save first; last resort only.
- An inbound DeathLink shows the game-over screen with no death animation.
- A summoned boat may face an odd direction at its pier.
- The overlay's counters can briefly disagree with the server. The server is
right.
- Hardcore and Professional runs have one Check fewer by design (a Bindery
stone the game will not hand over). If another stone there refuses to be
picked up, report it.
- Random Events are experimental. A moved Check keeps its name but not its old
spot; its Marker follows it.

pages.title: The World Patcher: BioRand
lines: The world you are fighting through - the enemies, the ambushes, the shape of
each seed - is the work of BioRand, the Resident Evil 4 randomizer by
IntelOrca. RE4R AP runs on a fork of it that takes its item placements from
the Multiworld.
Your settings file also decides how far BioRand randomizes weapon upgrades:
untouched, rerolled stats, or full random upgrade trees (recent upstream work
by Mark Parton made the middle option possible).
BioRand's own welcome note follows, as it was written.

pages.title: Welcome to BioRand 2.0
lines: Dear {slot},
Welcome to the 2.0 version of the Resident Evil 4 remake Randomizer. I'm
thrilled to see how popular this randomizer has become, and I'm deeply
grateful for the incredible support I have received for it.
With this new version, there are lots of new exciting features to keep you on
edge and surprise you with each seed.

pages.title: Random events
lines: Each seed will have a number of events that occur. You may occasionally find
yourself locked in a room or area forcing you to fight foes until the doors
unlock.
Keys will not always be where they normally are. Some will be held by a tough
enemy nearby, others will be completely relocated. Keep your eyes open for
files that provide clues.

pages.title: Rare legendary weapons
lines: Hidden within certain seeds are powerful, one-of-a-kind weapons. These weapons
contain powerful memes and unique mechanics.
Gun rhymes with fun for a reason.
